verses.zh: （亚萨的诗歌。）　神啊，求你不要静默！　神啊，求你不要闭口，也不要不作声！
verses.en: A song, a psalm of Asaph.O God, do not be silent.Do not ignore us.[NOTE:1] Do not be inactive, O God.
notes: Psalm 83. The psalmist asks God to deliver Israel from the attacks of foreign nations. Recalling how God defeated Israel’s enemies in the days of Deborah and Gideon, he prays that the hostile nations would be humiliated.

verses.zh: 因为你的仇敌喧嚷，恨你的抬起头来。
verses.en: For look, your enemies are making a commotion;those who hate you are hostile.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “do not be deaf.”

verses.zh: 他们同谋奸诈要害你的百姓，彼此商议要害你所隐藏的人。
verses.en: They carefully plot[NOTE:1] against your people,and make plans to harm[NOTE:2] the ones you cherish.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “lift up [their] head[s].” The phrase “lift up [the] head” here means “to threaten; to be hostile,” as in Judg 8:28.
Heb “they make crafty a plot.”
Heb “and consult together against.”

verses.zh: 他们说：来吧，我们将他们剪灭，使他们不再成国！使以色列的名不再被人记念！
verses.en: They say, “Come on, let’s annihilate them so they are no longer a nation.[NOTE:1] Then the name of Israel will be remembered no more.”
notes: The passive participle of the Hebrew verb צָפַן (tsafan, “to hide”) is used here in the sense of “treasured; cherished.”

verses.zh: 他们同心商议，彼此结盟，要抵挡你，
verses.en: Yes,[NOTE:1] they devise a unified strategy;[NOTE:2] they form an alliance[NOTE:3] against you.
notes: Heb “we will cause them to disappear from [being] a nation.”
Or “for.”
Heb “they consult [with] a heart together.”

verses.zh: 就是住帐棚的以东人和以实玛利人，摩押和夏甲人，
verses.en: It includes[NOTE:1] the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,Moab and the Hagrites,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “cut a covenant.”
The words “it includes” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 迦巴勒、亚扪，和亚玛力、非利士并泰尔的居民。
verses.en: Gebal,[NOTE:1] Ammon, and Amalek,Philistia, and the inhabitants of Tyre.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hagrites are also mentioned in 1 Chr 5:10, 19-20.

Some identify Gebal with the Phoenician coastal city of Byblos (see Ezek 27:9, where the name is spelled differently), though others locate this site south of the Dead Sea (see BDB 148 s.v. גְּבַל; HALOT 174 s.v. גְּבַל).

verses.zh: 亚述也与他们连合；他们作罗得子孙的帮手。（细拉）
verses.en: Even Assyria has allied with them,lending its strength to the descendants of Lot.[NOTE:1] (Selah)
notes: For location see Map1-A2; Map2-G2; Map4-A1; JP3-F3; JP4-F3.

verses.zh: 求你待他们，如待米甸，如在基顺河待西西拉和耶宾一样。
verses.en: Do to them as you did to Midian[NOTE:1]—as you did to Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River.[NOTE:2]
notes: The descendants of Lot were the Moabites and Ammonites.tn Heb “they are an arm for the sons of Lot.” The “arm” is here a symbol of military might.
Heb “do to them like Midian.”

verses.zh: 他们在隐・多珥灭亡，成了地上的粪土。
verses.en: They were destroyed at Endor;[NOTE:1] their corpses were like manure[NOTE:2] on the ground.
notes: The psalmist alludes here to Gideon’s victory over the Midianites (see Judg 7-8) and to Barak’s victory over Jabin’s army, which was led by his general Sisera (Judg 4-5).

Endor is not mentioned in the accounts of Gideon’s or Barak’s victories, but both battles took place in the general vicinity of the town. (See Y. Aharoni and M. Avi-Yonah, The Macmillan Bible Atlas, 46, 54.) Because Sisera and Jabin are mentioned in v. 9b, many understand them to be the subject of the verbs in v. 10, though they relate v. 10 to Gideon’s victory, which is referred to in v. 9a, 11. (See, for example, Y. Aharoni, The Land of the Bible, 263.)

verses.zh: 求你叫他们的首领像俄立和西伊伯，叫他们的王子都像西巴和撒慕拿。
verses.en: Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb,[NOTE:1] and all their rulers like Zebah and Zalmunna,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they were manure.” In addition to this passage, corpses are compared to manure in 2 Kgs 9:37; Jer 8:2; 9:21; 16:4; 25:33.
Oreb and Zeeb were the generals of the Midianite army that was defeated by Gideon. The Ephraimites captured and executed both of them and sent their heads to Gideon (Judg 7:24-25).

verses.zh: 他们说：我们要得　神的住处，作为自己的产业。
verses.en: who said,[NOTE:1] “Let’s take over[NOTE:2] the pastures of God.”
notes: Zebah and Zalmunna were the Midianite kings. Gideon captured them and executed them (Judg 8:1-21).

The translation assumes that “Zebah and Zalmunna” are the antecedents of the relative pronoun (“who [said]”). Another option is to take “their nobles…all their rulers” as the antecedent and to translate, “those who say.”

verses.zh: 我的　神啊，求你叫他们像旋风的尘土，像风前的碎秸。
verses.en: O my God, make them like dead thistles,[NOTE:1] like dead weeds blown away by[NOTE:2] the wind.
notes: Heb “let’s take possession for ourselves.”

Or “tumbleweed.” The Hebrew noun גַּלְגַּל (galgal) refers to a “wheel” or, metaphorically, to a whirling wind (see Ps 77:18). If taken in the latter sense here, one could understand the term as a metonymical reference to dust blown by a whirlwind (cf. NRSV “like whirling dust”). However, HALOT 190 s.v. II גַּלְגַּל understands the noun as a homonym referring to a “dead thistle” here and in Isa 17:13. The parallel line, which refers to קַשׁ (qash, “chaff”), favors this interpretation.

verses.zh: 火怎样焚烧树林，火焰怎样烧着山岭，
verses.en: Like the fire that burns down the forest,or the flames that consume the mountainsides,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “before.”

verses.zh: 求你也照样用狂风追赶他们，用暴雨恐吓他们。
verses.en: chase them with your gale windsand terrify[NOTE:1] them with your windstorm.
notes: The imagery of fire and flames suggests unrelenting, destructive judgment.

verses.zh: 愿你使他们满面羞耻，好叫他们寻求你―耶和华的名！
verses.en: Cover[NOTE:1] their faces with shame,so they might seek[NOTE:2] you,[NOTE:3] O Lord.
notes: The two imperfect verbal forms in v. 15 express the psalmist’s wish or prayer.
Heb “fill.”
After the preceding imperative, the prefixed verbal form with prefixed vav (ו) indicates purpose or result (“then they will seek”).

verses.zh: 愿他们永远羞愧惊惶！愿他们惭愧灭亡！
verses.en: May they be humiliated and continually terrified.[NOTE:1] May they die in shame.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your name,” which stands here for God’s person.

Heb “and may they be terrified to perpetuity.” The Hebrew expression עֲדֵי־עַד (ʿade ʿad, “to perpetuity”) can mean “forevermore” (see Pss 92:7; 132:12, 14), but here it may be used hyperbolically, for the psalmist asks that the experience of judgment might lead the nations to recognize (v. 18) and even to seek (v. 16) God.

verses.zh: 使他们知道：惟独你―名为耶和华的―是全地以上的至高者！
verses.en: Then they will know[NOTE:1] that you alone are the Lord,[NOTE:2] the Most High[NOTE:3] over all the earth.
notes: Heb “may they be ashamed and perish.” The four prefixed verbal forms in this verse are understood as jussives. The psalmist concludes his prayer with an imprecation, calling severe judgment down on his enemies. The strong language of the imprecation seems to run contrary to the positive outcome of divine judgment envisioned in v. 16b. Perhaps the language of v. 17 is overstated for effect. Another option is that v. 16b expresses an ideal, while the strong imprecation of vv. 17-18 anticipates reality. It would be nice if the defeated nations actually pursued a relationship with God, but if judgment does not bring them to that point, the psalmist asks that they be annihilated so that they might at least be forced to acknowledge God’s power.
After the preceding jussives (v. 17), the prefixed verbal form with prefixed vav (ו) indicates purpose (“so that they may know”) or result.
Heb “that you, your name [is] the Lord, you alone.”
